ActivitySeries.description:
Runs per day, split by environment.

Parallel arrays rather than a list of objects: every entry in ``days`` lines up with
the same index in each environment's list, which is the shape a chart wants and
avoids sending the date once per series.
ActivitySeries.title: ActivitySeries

AdjudicationRequest.description:
A human's ruling on a change the engine could not decide.

``reason`` is required. An adjudication without one cannot be used to tune the rule
set, which is the only reason the queue is worth anybody's time.
AdjudicationRequest.title: AdjudicationRequest

AffectedAccreditation.description:
An approval this change would move, named so the console can say whose it is.

A reviewer's first question about a material change is never "which rule fired" —
it is "who do I have to tell".
AffectedAccreditation.title: AffectedAccreditation

AgentHealth.description:
One word for whether an agent needs attention.

Four levels, not five, and no numeric score. A score invites arguing about the
formula instead of fixing the agent, and a fifth level always turns out to mean
"somewhere between the two I actually act on".
AgentHealth.title: AgentHealth

AgentOperations.description:
The estate's questions, asked of one agent.

Deliberately the same aggregates as :class:`OperationsSnapshot` rather than a smaller
bespoke set: someone looking at a single agent after seeing it on the dashboard is
checking the same numbers, and a detail page that computes them differently from the
overview is a page people learn not to trust.
AgentOperations.title: AgentOperations

AgentOpsRow.description:
One agent, with what it is and what it has been doing side by side.

The join this product exists to make. A runtime dashboard shows cost and latency; a
governance tool shows approvals and drift. Neither answers "is the expensive one also
the unapproved one", which is the question that changes what somebody does next.
AgentOpsRow.title: AgentOpsRow

AssessRequest.description:
Two descriptors, ruled without persisting anything.

Deliberately accepts raw descriptors rather than version ids: the CI gate runs
against a change that has not been deployed and may never be, so requiring a
registered version would defeat the purpose.

framework_slug.description: Rule under a specific framework rather than the agent's strictest.
framework_slug.title: Framework Slug

AssessRequest.title: AssessRequest

AssessmentOut.description: The result of ruling on a whole release.
AssessmentOut.title: AssessmentOut

AttentionItem.description:
One thing a person has to decide about, phrased as a consequence.

`consequence` is the field that earns this screen its place. "Northwind is running an
unapproved version" is a fact; "Northwind has not agreed to what is running for them"
is why anyone should stop what they are doing. A list of facts gets skimmed.
AttentionItem.title: AttentionItem

AuditDigest.description:
Counts for the security overview, over a bounded window.

Bounded because the aggregate is computed live: a window is a partition-pruned scan,
"all time" is not.
AuditDigest.title: AuditDigest

AuditQuery.description:
Filters for a keyset listing.

Every filter narrows an index the listing already uses. Deliberately no free-text
search: on a partitioned table with billions of rows an unindexed `ILIKE` is a way to
take the control plane down from the audit page.
AuditQuery.title: AuditQuery

AuditRecord.description:
One event, as a producer submits it.

There is no ``occurred_at``: the database stamps it. A caller-supplied timestamp on an
append-only log is a way to write history out of order, and the partition a row lands
in is decided by that column.
AuditRecord.title: AuditRecord

AuthConfigOut.description: The whole answer to "how do I sign in to this deployment?".
AuthConfigOut.title: AuthConfigOut

AuthProviderOut.description:
One sign-in button, as the login screen needs it.

``authorize_url``, ``client_id`` and ``scopes`` are public by construction — they
appear in the address bar of every sign-in. What is *not* here is everything the
browser used to read from its own build environment and get wrong.
AuthProviderOut.title: AuthProviderOut

BatchVerification.description: Result of re-deriving one batch from the events it claims to cover.

signature_valid.description: None when the batch carries no signature
signature_valid.title: Signature Valid

BatchVerification.title: BatchVerification

BootstrapAccess.description:
What you may do, flattened, and where.

``permissions`` answers "may this person ever"; ``scoped`` answers "may this person
here". The console uses the first to decide what to render and the second to decide
what to enable, and both come from the same evaluation so they cannot disagree.
BootstrapAccess.title: BootstrapAccess

BootstrapAccount.description: Which account, and what shape of install it is.
BootstrapAccount.title: BootstrapAccount

BootstrapMember.description:
Who you are. Deliberately not the full member record.

The profile page fetches the rest. What is here is what the shell paints: the avatar,
the name under it, and the identifiers every later request is attributed to.
BootstrapMember.title: BootstrapMember

BootstrapSession.description: When this session dies, so the console can renew before it does.
BootstrapSession.title: BootstrapSession

CapabilityDeclared.description:
One capability as the server advertised it.

``input_schema_digest`` is supplied by the discovery client, which hashes the schema
    canonically. Sending the schema itself would put arbitrary server-controlled JSON of
    unbounded size into a control-plane table for no decision-making benefit.
CapabilityDeclared.title: CapabilityDeclared

CapabilityReview.description:
A human's verdict on what a tool actually does.

Separate from the declared annotations on purpose: an MCP server declares its own
``destructiveHint``, and a server that lies about it is precisely the case this
registry exists to catch.
CapabilityReview.title: CapabilityReview

Category.description:
The tab an event appears under in the console.

A closed set rather than free text. An auditor filtering for "everything that touched
access control last quarter" needs the category to mean the same thing in January as
in December, which free-text strings do not survive.
Category.title: Category

ChainVerification.description:
Whole-chain result. This is what the trust portal renders, and what an auditor
is really asking for when they ask whether the log can be trusted.
ChainVerification.title: ChainVerification

ChangeCategory.description: What kind of thing changed. Drives grouping in the release view.
ChangeCategory.title: ChangeCategory

ComplianceBar.description:
One governance ratio, with the two numbers it came from.

`covered` and `applicable` travel with the percentage on purpose: "80%" means
something very different at four agents than at four hundred, and a bar without its
denominator is the kind of number that gets quoted in a board pack unchallenged.
ComplianceBar.title: ComplianceBar

ConnectionRotate.description:
Point the connection at new material.

Takes a reference, never a value. The gateway resolves the reference through
``app/providers``, so this endpoint can be called by somebody who is allowed to
rotate a key without being allowed to read one.
ConnectionRotate.title: ConnectionRotate

ControlGap.description: A control this client demands that no evidence kind currently answers.
ControlGap.title: ControlGap

CostSlice.description: Cost attributed to one thing — a model, an agent, an environment.
CostSlice.title: CostSlice

CriticalityTier.description:
How much rigour this client's review demands.

Drives default frameworks, probe frequency, and whether a conditional accreditation
is acceptable at all. Tier 1 is a client whose own regulator will eventually read
the pack.
CriticalityTier.title: CriticalityTier

CrossBorderTransfer.description:
Ordered least to most permissive, matching ``_CROSS_BORDER_LADDER``.

Safeguards and consent are separate rungs because they are separate bases under
GDPR Chapter V: Article 46 safeguards persist with the data, Article 49 consent
authorises the transfer and then protects nothing. See D-020.
CrossBorderTransfer.title: CrossBorderTransfer

CustomerReadiness.description:
Can we even attempt this client's review, and where will we fall short?

Computable from the company model alone, before a single evidence event exists,
which makes it the first genuinely useful screen in the product: it turns "we will
find out during the review" into a number known at onboarding.

gaps.description: Unmapped mandatory controls, worst first. The work queue.
gaps.title: Gaps

CustomerReadiness.title: CustomerReadiness

CustomerSummary.description:
List-view row. Flat, and every count is a roll-up so the list needs no joins
per row.
CustomerSummary.title: CustomerSummary

CustomerUpdate.description:
Every field optional. Slug is absent deliberately: it appears in URLs and in
generated pack filenames, so renaming one would orphan existing references.
CustomerUpdate.title: CustomerUpdate

DriftItem.description: One client being served a version they have not approved.
DriftItem.title: DriftItem

DriftResponse.description:
Wraps the report so ``headline`` crosses the wire.

Pydantic does not serialise ``@property``, and a console that recomputes the
sentence will eventually word it differently from the accreditation pack.
DriftResponse.title: DriftResponse

DriftSeverity.description:
How bad it is that a client is being served an unapproved version.

``none`` still appears in responses rather than being filtered out, so the console
can show a green row instead of an absence and leave no doubt it was checked.
DriftSeverity.title: DriftSeverity

DriftStatus.description: Whether what is running matches what was signed off as the baseline.
DriftStatus.title: DriftStatus

EffectiveAccess.description:
What one member may actually do, flattened.

    ``permissions`` is the union across every live grant. ``scoped`` answers the narrower
question the enforcement path asks: this permission, on this resource.
EffectiveAccess.title: EffectiveAccess

EnforcementLevel-Input.description: Gradual rollout: advisory records, blocking refuses dispatch at the gateway.
EnforcementLevel-Input.title: EnforcementLevel

EngagementSummary.description: List-row shape. The three counts are what makes the list worth reading.
EngagementSummary.title: EngagementSummary

EngagementUpdate.description:
Every field optional. ``exclude_unset`` in the service distinguishes "set to
null" from "not mentioned", which a PATCH must not conflate.
EngagementUpdate.title: EngagementUpdate

ErrorKindCount.description: Why runs failed. A classification, never a message — see `AgentRun.error_kind`.
ErrorKindCount.title: ErrorKindCount

EstateTotals.description: Counts for the estate as a whole. Every one of these is a link to a screen.
EstateTotals.title: EstateTotals

lawful_basis.description: data_class -> lawful basis label, required for special-category classes
lawful_basis.title: Lawful Basis

EvidenceBatchRequest.description:
Bulk ingest. The collector buffers to local disk during an outage, so a
reconnect commonly delivers thousands at once.
EvidenceBatchRequest.title: EvidenceBatchRequest

EvidenceKind.description:
Names the *fact being evidenced*, not the mechanism that observed it.

Mechanism belongs in ``detected_by``: the same fact arriving from a span, a
Kubernetes scan or a manual upload is one label rather than three.
EvidenceKind.title: EvidenceKind

EvidenceRecord.description:
One event offered for ingest.

Field lengths mirror the CHECK constraints in migration 0003. Validating here as
well means a caller gets a 422 naming the field rather than a 500 from a constraint
violation, which matters because the most common cause is a collector trying to
send something it should not.
EvidenceRecord.title: EvidenceRecord

is_builtin.description: True when we shipped it (org_id IS NULL)
is_builtin.title: Is Builtin

is_builtin.description: False when this tenant authored it
is_builtin.title: Is Builtin

scoped_controls.description: Empty means the whole framework. Clients often scope to a subset.
scoped_controls.title: Scoped Controls

FrameworkShare.description:
How much of the estate is built on one agent framework.

"Framework" here means LangGraph, CrewAI, the Cursor SDK — the thing the agent's code
is written against. Not to be confused with the compliance frameworks in
``domains/frameworks``, which are ISO 42001 and the like. The column behind this is
``agent_versions.runtime_framework``, and the API path says ``runtime`` for the same
reason.
FrameworkShare.title: FrameworkShare

FrameworkSuggestion.description: Offered on customer creation so nobody picks from a list of forty.

confidence.description: strong when sector and jurisdiction both match
confidence.title: Confidence

reason.description: Why this was suggested, shown next to the checkbox
reason.title: Reason

FrameworkSuggestion.title: FrameworkSuggestion

is_builtin.description: True when we shipped it (org_id IS NULL)
is_builtin.title: Is Builtin

GatewayTargetKind.description: Pluggable enforcement point — LiteLLM is the first supported emitter.
GatewayTargetKind.title: GatewayTargetKind

GrantSummary.description: A grant with the display labels the console needs, resolved server-side.
GrantSummary.title: GrantSummary

HomeSummary.description:
Everything the landing page shows, in one request.

It grew. The previous version answered only "is anything wrong", on the argument
that every breakdown has a screen of its own — which was right for a console with no
runtime data in it, and stopped being right once there was. An estate's cost, its
failure rate and which framework it runs on are not follow-up questions; they are the
first thing anyone asks, and making each one a separate navigation is how a dashboard
ends up being opened once and never again.

Still one request. The alternative is seven, arriving in an order the user can watch,
which reads as a slow page rather than a rich one.
HomeSummary.title: HomeSummary

IdentityBind.description:
Bind a verified IdP subject to a member.

    ``issuer`` and ``subject`` come from a token this service verified, never from a
request body field a client chose — the router takes them from the caller's own claims
    when self-binding, and an identity admin supplies them only for directory import.
IdentityBind.title: IdentityBind

ImpactDimension.description:
Why a reader should care. A release view shows these as badges, which is what
lets someone triage twenty releases without reading any of them in full.
ImpactDimension.title: ImpactDimension

InclusionProof.description:
Proof that one event is in a published root.

The audit path carries sibling *digests*, so handing this to a customer discloses
nothing about any other event — which is what makes it safe to publish per-event
proofs to a shared trust portal.
InclusionProof.title: InclusionProof

McpServerRow.description:
One MCP server, with everything the estate called through it.

Reported separately from the tool list because the server is the thing somebody
owns, patches and can revoke. When an MCP server misbehaves the action is at this
level — disconnect it, pin it, ask its operator — not at the level of one tool.
McpServerRow.title: McpServerRow

MemberProfile.description:
Everything the signed-in person's own profile page needs, in one response.

Deliberately not assembled from four endpoints on the client. The profile page is the
first thing rendered after login, and four sequential requests there is four times
the latency for no benefit.
MemberProfile.title: MemberProfile

MemberSummary.description:
A member plus the derived facts the console list actually renders.

    Team names and role keys are joined in one query rather than fetched per row: a
thousand-member account otherwise produces a thousand round trips to draw one table.
MemberSummary.title: MemberSummary

environment.description: Agent version environment; production triggers fail-closed rules.
environment.title: Environment

ModuleAccessOut.description: Effective capability after licence expiry and per-module grace rules.
ModuleAccessOut.title: ModuleAccessOut

revision.description: sha256:… over the canonical effective manifest body.
revision.title: Revision

NavItem.description:
One link. The server has already decided you may see it.

``icon`` is a name, not a glyph: the client owns the icon set, and shipping SVG in a
JSON envelope would couple the API to a component library's version.

``matches`` exists because several links own more than one route subtree — the
assurance entry covers five. Active state is computed from ``path`` plus these, by
matching the URL, never from React state. Deriving it from state is what made one
click highlight three tabs.
NavItem.title: NavItem

OperationsSnapshot.description:
Everything operations knows about the window, for the console's landing page.

Composed into the home summary rather than served to the dashboard directly, because
the dashboard also needs findings, approvals and service levels — and those belong to
other domains. ``home`` is the only module allowed to know about all of them.
OperationsSnapshot.title: OperationsSnapshot

ProbeCaseResultOut.description: One probe row — oracle and judge counts stay on separate fields.
ProbeCaseResultOut.title: ProbeCaseResultOut

ProductModeOut.description:
Which product the console leads with.

Not a theme and not a permission. It selects the information architecture: a
``ledger`` console puts agent actions first and leaves the accreditation screens
reachable by URL, an ``assurance`` console does the reverse. Both render the same
routes from the same `App.tsx`; only the navigation and the home screen differ.
ProductModeOut.title: ProductModeOut

answerable.description: At least one control mapping exists
answerable.title: Answerable

partial.description: Mapped, but no mapping claims full satisfaction
partial.title: Partial

unmapped.description: Nothing in the platform answers this yet
unmapped.title: Unmapped

ReadinessResponse.description:
Wraps the model so the computed properties cross the wire.

Pydantic does not serialise ``@property``, and a client that has to recompute
coverage will eventually compute it differently from the console.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ReleaseGateVerdict.description:
Returned to CI before a deploy. The reason the platform gets adopted by
engineering rather than only by governance.

affected_accreditations.description: Accreditation references that this release would suspend
affected_accreditations.title: Affected Accreditations

ReleaseGateVerdict.title: ReleaseGateVerdict

ReleasePreviewRequest.description: CI gate input — no persisted agent required.
ReleasePreviewRequest.title: ReleasePreviewRequest

ReleaseReviewBrief.description: Structured summary for a non-technical approver — derived on read, never LLM-sourced.
ReleaseReviewBrief.title: ReleaseReviewBrief

ReleaseSummary.description: List-view row. Deliberately flat so the release list needs no joins.
ReleaseSummary.title: ReleaseSummary

reviewed_descriptor_digest.description: Required when approving; must match the target version digest reviewed
reviewed_descriptor_digest.title: Reviewed Descriptor Digest

ResolvedConnection.description:
What the gateway needs to actually make a call, for one subject and environment.

Returned only to a workload-authenticated caller. It carries the credential
*reference*, which the gateway exchanges for material through its own secret provider
— so a leak of this response does not leak a key.
ResolvedConnection.title: ResolvedConnection

ReviewQueueItem.description:
A change awaiting human adjudication.

Ordered by consequence rather than by arrival: a needs-review change on an approved
accreditation for a tier-one client is not the same as one on a development agent,
and a queue sorted by timestamp buries the first behind the second.
ReviewQueueItem.title: ReviewQueueItem

ReviewSentence.description: One deterministic plain-language line in the review brief.
ReviewSentence.title: ReviewSentence

RoleCreate.description: A tenant-defined role. Built-in roles are seeded by migration and immutable.
RoleCreate.title: RoleCreate

RoutingOverview.description: Console summary — catalogue health, recent denials, drift signals.

observation_note.default: Observed models from run steps detect drift only; they do not block requests.
observation_note.title: Observation Note

RoutingOverview.title: RoutingOverview

RuleOut.description:
One rule, as the settings screen and the accreditation pack render it.

A customer asked to accept automated suspension wants to read the rules before
agreeing, so ``rationale`` is written for them rather than for us.
RuleOut.title: RuleOut

RunBatch.title: RunBatch

RunOutcome.description:
How a run ended, or that it has not.

``refused`` is separate from ``failed`` on purpose. An agent declining to act,
because a guardrail fired or a policy denied it, is the system working as designed;
counting it as a failure makes a well-governed estate look broken and gives people a
reason to turn the guardrail off.
RunOutcome.title: RunOutcome

RunReport.description:
One run, as an SDK or collector reports it.

The same report is used to open a run and to close it: send it with no ``ended_at``
when work starts, then again with the outcome when it finishes. ``run_id`` is chosen
by the client so the second report can find the first, and so a retried delivery is
recognised rather than counted twice.

An agent is named either by ``agent_id`` or by ``agent_urn``. The URN is what an SDK
knows — it comes from configuration next to the agent's own code — whereas the id is
a database key the agent has no reason to hold.
RunReport.title: RunReport

RunRow.description: One run for a list view, carrying enough about its agent to render a row.
RunRow.title: RunRow

ScopedAgentOut.description:
One agent in scope for one engagement, with both versions resolved to labels.

Carrying the semver strings rather than only the version ids is deliberate: the
console's whole job on this screen is to let a human see "approved 2.1, running
2.4" without a second request per row.
ScopedAgentOut.title: ScopedAgentOut

reason.description: Why nothing was sealed, when batch is None
reason.title: Reason

Sector.description:
Constrained because sector selects the default framework set. A bank and a
hospital ask for different evidence, and free text cannot drive that.
Sector.title: Sector

SemanticChange.description: One high-level change. Produced by the differ, never written by hand.

detail.description: Optional consequence explanation, e.g. why a shorter timeout matters
detail.title: Detail

summary.description: The one-line sentence shown in the release view
summary.title: Summary

SemanticChange.title: SemanticChange

ServerDetail.description:
Everything the server page renders, in one response.

The console's MCP page shows the server, its approved capability list, its grants and
its recent usage together. Four endpoints would mean four sequential requests for one
view, and the drift banner needs the approved and observed snapshots side by side to
say anything true.
ServerDetail.title: ServerDetail

SessionOut.description: Confirmation that a session now exists. The token itself is only ever a cookie.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SessionStart.description:
What the callback screen posts. One shape for every provider kind.

Validation is per kind rather than "all fields optional": a development sign-in that
silently ignored a missing ``code`` would be indistinguishable from an OIDC one that
lost it, and those want opposite fixes.
SessionStart.title: SessionStart

SnapshotCompileRequest.description: Optional override; default TTL comes from settings.
SnapshotCompileRequest.title: SnapshotCompileRequest

SnapshotSubmit.description: A discovery result. Recorded whether or not it matches the approved snapshot.
SnapshotSubmit.title: SnapshotSubmit

StepKind.description: What one row in ``run_steps`` represents — a graph node, a model call, a tool.
StepKind.title: StepKind

StepReport.description: One step inside a run, as a LangGraph callback would report it.
StepReport.title: StepReport

enabled.description: Signed entitlement — module purchased and declared on.
enabled.title: Enabled

ToolCallReport.description:
Tool activity from one run, already counted.

A run reports its tool calls as totals rather than individually, because that is
what the daily buckets store and what every screen asks for. A LangGraph callback
handler naturally accumulates exactly this.
ToolCallReport.title: ToolCallReport

ToolDecision.description:
The gateway's answer for one attempted tool call.

``allowed`` is the only field the gateway must honour. The rest exists so the denial
is explainable: an operator looking at a blocked call should be able to see which
grant was missing or which snapshot was stale without reading a policy bundle.
ToolDecision.title: ToolDecision

ToolDecisionRequest.description:
Ask whether a tool call is permitted.

The subject is not in this model. It comes from the verified workload credential, so
a caller cannot ask "may *somebody else* call this" and act on the answer.
ToolDecisionRequest.title: ToolDecisionRequest

ToolRow.description: One tool, aggregated across every agent that called it in the window.
ToolRow.title: ToolRow

ToolSurface.description:
Where a tool came from.

``MCP`` is the one this product cares most about: an MCP server is a dependency with
its own supply chain, and the tools it exposes can change without the agent's
descriptor changing at all.
ToolSurface.title: ToolSurface

UsageIngest.description:
One day's aggregate for one capability, from the worker.

    Aggregates, never individual calls. At the volumes this platform targets a per-call
control-plane row is not an option; the per-call record lives in ClickHouse behind
    Observe and this is the rollup the console and the grant reviewer read.
UsageIngest.title: UsageIngest

VersionUptake.description:
Whether a client accepts new agent versions without a fresh review.

``pinned`` is the default everywhere. A client who has not said otherwise has not
consented to receiving a version they have not seen.
VersionUptake.title: VersionUptake

WorkloadCredentialCreated.description: Returned once on create or rotate — the only time the secret is visible.
WorkloadCredentialCreated.title: WorkloadCredentialCreated

app__domains__auth__schemas__SessionSumm.description: One row in "your sessions" on the profile page.
app__domains__auth__schemas__SessionSumm.title: SessionSummary

app__domains__engagements__schemas__Drif.description:
Estate-wide drift, worst first.

``clean`` is reported alongside the drifting rows because the useful statement to a
client is "142 of 147 deliveries are serving exactly what you approved", and that
sentence needs the denominator.
app__domains__engagements__schemas__Drif.title: DriftReport

app__domains__model_routing__schemas__En.description: Gradual rollout: advisory records, blocking refuses dispatch at the gateway.
app__domains__model_routing__schemas__En.title: EnforcementLevel

app__domains__releases__schemas__Enforce.description: How strongly a change blocks rollout — advisory, overrideable, or hard.
app__domains__releases__schemas__Enforce.title: EnforcementLevel

info.description: Discovery, release intelligence, accreditation and continuous attestation for enterprise AI agents.
info.title: Agent Assurance Platform

get.description:
Liveness. Must not touch the database — a database blip should not cause an
orchestrator to kill an otherwise healthy process.
Readiness. Reports everything an operator of a self-hosted install needs.

post.summary: Grant a role at a scope

Deliberately unguarded beyond authentication.

Anybody may ask what they themselves can do — the console needs it to decide which
navigation to render, and refusing it would mean showing every user every destination
and letting them discover the 403s by clicking.

post.description:
Any authenticated member may ask. Asking is not access.

Guarded by nothing but authentication on purpose: a request the requester cannot make
is a request they will make by email instead, and then no record of it exists.

get.description:
The security overview's headline figures, over a bounded window.

Computed live rather than cached, which is affordable only because the window prunes
to one or two monthly partitions. That is why `days` has a ceiling.

Newest-first, keyset-paginated.

There is no page number and no total. `OFFSET n` makes Postgres produce and discard
`n` rows, so on this table the cost of a page would grow with how deep the reader has
gone; a cursor is an index seek at any depth. The response carries `next_cursor` or
nothing, which is what a keyset listing can honestly say.

post.description:
Enforcement decisions made outside the API, appended to the same trail.

The gateway denies a tool call in the data path and the console must be able to show
that denial next to the grant change that caused it. Both therefore land in one table.

The organisation comes from the presented credential, never from a header: a workload
must not be able to write events into another tenant's evidence.

schema.title: Response Submit Events V1 Audit Events Post

post.summary: Submit audit events (gateway and worker path)

get.description:
The history panel on a server, connection or member page.

Its own route rather than a filter on the listing because `target_id` has a dedicated
index; routing it through the general endpoint would leave the choice of index to
whichever other filters the caller happened to include.
get.summary: Everything that happened to one resource

get.description:
Unauthenticated by necessity: it is read before anybody can be authenticated.

Returns no secrets. ``client_id`` and ``authorize_url`` are in the address bar of
every sign-in that has ever happened; ``client_secret_ref``, ``token_url``,
``jwks_uri`` and ``claim_map`` are not in the response model at all.
get.summary: Which sign-in methods this deployment offers

post.description:
Revokes the row first, clears the cookie second.

That order matters if the second step fails: a revoked row with a stale cookie is a
session that no longer works, and a live row with no cookie is a session somebody
else's copy of the token can still use.
Slides the idle window forward. Never moves the absolute ceiling.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for a console session

get.summary: Where you are currently signed in

delete.summary: Revoke one of your own sessions

get.summary: Which agents depend on a named component

post.description:
Records a reference to the customer's own credential, never the credential.

``credential_ref`` names a secret in the customer's provider — a Vault path, a KMS
key id, or an env var in a local install. Whoever calls this does not need to be able

schema.title: Response List Grants V1 Mcp Servers  Server Id  Grants Get

post.description:
Pinned to the currently approved snapshot unless the caller opts out.

Without pinning, a grant reads whichever snapshot is approved at call time, so a
server that adds a tool and gets re-approved would hand that tool to every existing
grant. Pinning is what makes new capabilities require a new decision.
post.summary: Grant access to a server or one capability

post.description:
One write, and the next tool call against this server is denied.

Grants are left intact. Revoking them one by one is the slow version of the same
intent and loses the state needed to restore access afterwards.

Record what a server currently advertises.

Idempotent by content: re-submitting an unchanged capability set returns the existing
snapshot with a fresh `discovered_at` rather than adding a row. A server polled every
five minutes for a year therefore produces one snapshot, not a hundred thousand.

Recording is not approving. A submission that differs from the approved snapshot
flips the server's health to `drift` and waits for a reviewer.

Make this snapshot the one grants resolve against.

Grants pinned to the previous snapshot keep resolving against it. That is deliberate:
approving a new capability set must not silently widen access somebody already
reviewed. Re-pinning those grants is a separate, visible decision.
